layers.message: Replace rate cache with TTL and size limit

prompt.utterance: Why did the author choose this cache strategy?

graderOnly: The only cache in the project is RateCache in fxrates/cache.py. Commit 'Initial currency conversion package' introduced it as a plain dict with no expiry and no size limit.

Commit 'Replace rate cache with TTL and size limit' (the third commit, before the STANDARDS install) changed it to an OrderedDict cache whose entries expire after 300 seconds (time.monotonic) and which evicts the least recently used pair when more than 256 pairs are held; it also added tests/test_cache.py.
Commit 'Document rate caching in README' only describes the TTL and size limit and how to change them; it gives no reason.

No ADR, design note, changelog, code comment, commit body, or other record states why the author chose TTL plus LRU, so the author's motive is unknown. Plausible benefits (fresher exchange rates, bounded memory) are inferences, not evidence of intent.
All commits share the builder's fixed timestamp, so 'when' the strategy changed is identified by commit order and hash, not by distinct dates.

vars.CACHE_COMMIT: ${COMMIT:Replace rate cache with TTL and size limit}

all.why: an answer that cites inspected source names the cache module

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

selfChecks.why: the project's tests (conversion, rounding, TTL expiry, LRU eviction) pass
history shows the commit where the cache strategy changed

selfChecks.cmd: sh -c 'test -z $(git log --format=%b -- fxrates tests README.md | tr -d [:space:]) && test ! -e docs && ! grep -rqi -e because -e rationale -e decided -e adr README.md fxrates tests'
selfChecks.why: no commit body, ADR folder, or project text records a motive for the cache strategy

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture, default installed workflow state (AUDITING, no cycle), so check is ok. Four pre-install commits build the history of a small Python package fxrates: 50 initial package with RateCache as an unbounded dict; 51 unrelated rounding options (history noise); 52 replaces RateCache with TTL (300 s) plus LRU (256 entries) and adds tests/test_cache.py; 53 documents the cache settings in README without rationale. Commit messages are subject-only and state what changed, never why. No ADR, docs folder, changelog, or comments give a motive. Compromise: all commits share the builder's fixed date, so 'when' is visible as commit order/hash rather than distinct timestamps.
